maria: Heads up — saw a noticeable spike in partial WS frames and chunk latency in prod between ~02:10–02:30 UTC. Got an alert but need pointers: where are the most reliable dashboards/traces/log queries for streaming chunk timing + disconnect causes? cc @kevin @jon

alerts-bot: [ALERT] streaming.partial_frames rate > 0.5% (5m) — fired at 2026-03-16T02:12:09Z. Alert link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/streaming.partial_frames/1854321987 :rotating_light:

kevin: Dashboard is the best start — https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/streaming-overview?orgId=1 (panel: Chunk timing, panel: WS disconnects). For traces use Jaeger -> service=runtime. Quick Loki query that helps filter partial frames + disconnects:

```
{job="runtime"} |= "partial_frame" or |= "ws_disconnect" | json | line_format "ts={{.ts}} req_id={{.req_id}} event={{.event}} latency={{.latency_ms}}"
```

kevin: Also add `kv_cache_miss=true` to the filter if you think prefix cache misses are involved. The chunk timing panel is backed by p95/p99 histograms; look at p50->p99 to see if it’s a tail issue.

jon: Do we have any example trace/request ids from the alert? that helps point to whether it's a router, gRPC, or model backend issue.

maria: Pulled one trace id from the alert event: `trace-0a1b2c3d4e`. Minimal log snippet I grabbed: 

```
2026-03-16T02:11:58.123Z req=abc123 evt=stream_chunk_send latency_ms=612 partial_frame=true kv_cache_miss=false node=runtime-12
2026-03-16T02:12:01.987Z req=abc123 evt=ws_disconnect code=1006 reason="connection reset by peer" node=runtime-12
2026-03-16T02:12:02.010Z req=def456 evt=stream_chunk_send latency_ms=130 partial_frame=false kv_cache_miss=true node=runtime-09
```

priya: Thanks — I can pull `prefix_cache.hit_rate` and `kv_cache.latency` for the 02:00–02:40 window and correlate with node IDs. I'll check Redis/ML-serving RPC tail latencies. I can join the on-call channel in 10m.

kevin: For alert tuning: current rule is a simple rate-based check on `streaming.partial_frames`. That's noisy for normal bursts. Proposal: change to a compound rule: fire when `rate(partial_frames[5m]) > 0.5%` AND `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(chunk_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 400` ms. That should reduce alerts when partials are low-latency.

maria: Sounds good. Where do we submit the alert change?

kevin: Open a PR against infra/monitoring - link: https://git.redwood/internal/infra/monitoring/tree and reference incident `INC-1234`. We keep runbook/edit notes in `/docs/oncall/streaming.md`.

maria: Perfect. I'll file the incident, paste these traces, and assign follow-ups. Thanks all :pray:

jon: If anyone ends up reproducing, leave a short reproducer (req id + curl/websocket snippet) in the ticket so QA can run it later.

priya: Will do. Posting results in INC-1234 by EOD.
